title: Credit Card Input UX Tips
summary: Learn how to optimize credit card input fields with smart formatting, brand detection, and patient validation. These UX tips help reduce user errors and friction during the checkout process.

transcript.text: Type 16 digits. Watch them become a card.
Raw digits are a blur. Group them four by four as they type. 16 numbers turn into a card you can read.
The first digit names the brand. 4 is Visa, 5 is Mastercard. Show the logo the instant it's known.
Insert a space and the cursor jumps back. Smart fields hold the caret where the finger left it. Nothing feels worse than retyping.
Don't flag an error on the first keystroke. Validate on blur, forgive while they type. Red means done and wrong, not unfinished.
Someone pastes a number full of dashes. Strip the noise and reformat it. Never reject a value you could clean yourself.
Format what they see. Store the raw digits underneath. The mask is for humans, the value is for code.
Follow for more form UX. Save this for your next checkout.

on_screen_text: Keep the caret where it was
before_after: Transforms a basic, error-prone text input into a smart, formatted credit card field that handles brand detection and data cleaning.
